intro: A weekly reading for the metro, mood-pieces more than predictions. Refreshed every Monday.

horoscopes.text: The plan you made on Sunday holds up under contact. Patience pays out at a rate you would not have predicted. Outside, the kind of warmth you don't notice you needed. A long exhale, an open window, a closed laptop.
You move through the day like someone who knows where the shortcuts are. A craving turns out to be hunger, then the right meal. Light one candle, no more.
Today, the small talk is good. You tell a story better than you have told it before. Somewhere near a back booth at the CC Club. The night is for listening, not talking.
The weather and your mood are in unusual agreement. A meal with one other person does most of the work this week. Outside, an east wind off the river. A handwritten note before sleep.
You walk into the room and the room knows. A photograph circulates without you knowing. People say nice things. Put the phone down. People will still be talking tomorrow.

A small repair, twenty minutes, large gain. You finish the puzzle you have been carrying around in your head. Outside, one of those days where the light does most of the work. A long shower. A short list for tomorrow.
A flower in a window catches you off guard. You see both sides and pick one anyway. Set the table for tomorrow's breakfast.
A truth you suspected gets confirmed, casually. Someone shows their hand, accidentally. You file it. A long exhale and a closed laptop.
You make a plan that involves leaving the metro before fall. A friend you have not seen since college sends a real message. Outside, a heavy late-afternoon stillness. Stop planning. Sleep.

You answer the email you have been dreading. It is not as bad as you thought. A long-stalled meeting finally happens. It was worth waiting for. Somewhere near the booth nearest the door at Mickey's Diner. Close the laptop. The week is long.
You see the system clearly. Most people do not. A friend takes your strange idea seriously. Somewhere near a bench at Loring Park. You were curious enough today. Rest.
A poem you read once comes back, half-remembered, helpful. A friend cries to you. You hold the room well. Outside, the kind of warmth you don't notice you needed. Set the phone face-down.
